slides.texte_overlay:
7 social hacks that feel like
cheating with new people
New gym, new café, new office? Learn the name of the person at the front desk and use it next time. "Morning, Luis." Within a week, you're the guy everyone in the place seems to know.
Want to join a conversation that's already going? Wait for a laugh, then ask "Okay, what did I miss?" Everyone loves retelling a good joke, and you're in without interrupting anything.
No idea what to say to someone new? Comment on something you're both looking at. "This line is moving at a historic pace." Shared situations are the easiest way in, and they never feel forced.

Keep a few great stories in your pocket. Five minutes a day of history, art or science. "Did you know Napoleon was once attacked by a crowd of rabbits?" New people remember the guy with the weird stories.
slides.texte_sophia: Keep a few great stories in your pocket. A micro-learning app like the Sophia app gives you five minutes a day of history, art or science. New people remember the guy with the weird stories.

slides.texte_overlay: Not sure they remember your name? Just say it again. "Hey, it's Alex, we met at Sarah's." You save them the panic of guessing, and they'll be relieved and grateful at the same time.
Someone tells you about their hobby? Ask them to teach you one thing. "Okay, show me how you'd tie that knot." People light up when they get to teach, and you skip ten polite questions.
Swapping numbers? Text right away with a detail. "Alex, the guy who hates cilantro." Now they know exactly who you are, instead of finding a random number in their phone three weeks later.
